requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
The implementation covers the core of `requirements.ci.span`, but I found one unspecified, untested behavior, so I'm marking it false. It is a small gap.

**What is implemented and covered**
- `definition_blocks` (src/lib.rs:508) and `colon_fence` (src/lib.rs:652) detect an opening fence of three or more colons followed by `{req}` and a name.
  - A closing fence is a colon-only line with at least as many colons as the opener, outside Markdown code blocks.
  - The body runs from the line after the opener to the start of the closing fence. Fenced code, headings and blank lines stay inside the body.
  - Anything after the closing fence is excluded, because the block `end` is the end of the closing line.
- `collect_definitions` (src/evidence.rs:402) trims the body text before it is compared with the evidence. A missing closing fence is reported as an error.
- Tests:
  - `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` (src/evidence.rs:1694) checks a body containing a code fence with `:::` inside it, an ATX heading and a setext heading. It also checks that text after the closing fence is excluded and that a second requirement is parsed separately.
  - `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` (src/lib.rs:1108) checks a longer fence that contains a shorter nested directive.
  - `reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence` (src/evidence.rs:1727) checks the missing-closing-fence error.
  - `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` (src/evidence.rs:1474) checks that a body containing a code fence matches the evidence.

**Gap**
- `colon_fence` accepts up to three leading spaces before both the opening and the closing fence (`trim_start_matches(' ')` with a limit of 3). The requirement says the opening fence is "immediately followed by `{req} <name>`" and says nothing about indentation. The related requirements, `fence_lengths` and `markdown_literals`, don't specify it either. No test exercises indented fences. This is behavior the requirement doesn't define, and it is unverified.
- Less important: no test checks that a colon line with trailing text is not treated as a closing fence. The closing-fence rule also tolerates trailing whitespace, which the requirement doesn't mention.

There are no FIXME markers acknowledging these points, so FIXME doesn't apply.

text: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.

A `{req}` opening fence MAY contain four or more colons. Habeas MUST accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener MUST remain inside the requirement body, allowing a nested colon directive. A closing fence outside a fenced code example with at least as many colons as the opener MUST end the body.

In Markdown, escaped roles and role-looking text in inline code, fenced code, or raw HTML MUST remain literal and MUST NOT count as references. A `{req}` directive inside a fenced code example and a legacy inline `{req}` role MUST NOT define a requirement.
